Preconditions:
[PRE:CLEAR_SESSION]

Baseline per-org OrganizationMembership.Status is Approved on both (declared explicitly) and Contact.Status is Approved, so the effective status resolves to Approved in both orgs; both are unlocked.
2. FRONTEND LANE fixture — a concurrently running backend-lane case must never bind the same alias, because an OrganizationMembership row is the mutable state this case writes.
3. READ-ONLY for this case (a write silently changes another lane's outcome): Organization.Roles, organization status, the store settings Customer.ContactDefaultStatus / Customer.OrganizationDefaultStatus, and the OrganizationRolesWhitelist / MembershipRolesWhitelist module settings. Snapshot Organization.Roles at the moment of use; never write it.
4. Build under test: VirtoCommerce.Customer 3.1021.0-pr-312-2605 or later (the build that introduces OrganizationAccessResolver and makes OrganizationIdClaimProvider delegate to it).
5. A /connect/token password grant on this environment REQUIRES storeId (camelCase) alongside the optional organization_id (snake_case); a grant without storeId returns HTTP 400 invalid_grant.
6. DISCRIMINATION REQUIREMENT (Step-4 gate finding, 2026-08-03) — this verdict is only meaningful when contact.currentOrganizationId names the org this case BLOCKS. A control token taken at an untouched fixture baseline (currentOrganizationId = a HEALTHY org, defaultOrganizationId = null) resolved that healthy org at TIER 1, and tier 1 selects the same org on the UNFILTERED pre-fix resolver too — so blocking a NON-pinned org PASSES ON A BROKEN BUILD and proves nothing. The pin is therefore set explicitly in Steps with a read-back, never inherited from the fixture baseline.
7. contact.currentOrganizationId IS writable and resettable via PUT {{BACK_URL}}/api/contacts (HTTP 204) — there is NO one-way door. Restoring it is this case's own responsibility, not a later re-seed's.
AXIS DISAMBIGUATION — three different fields are called "status"; every step below names the one it writes and the endpoint that writes it:
  (i) ApplicationUser.Status (security account: Approved / Locked / EmailUnconfirmed / PendingApproval) — seeded from b2b/users.csv and hardcoded 'Approved' by seedMemberships. NOT written by any case here.
  (ii) Contact.Status (global member: New / Approved / Rejected / Deleted / Invited / Locked) — not seeded; written on the contact record via the member API (GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/members/<contactId>, merge, PUT {{BACK_URL}}/api/contacts).
  (iii) OrganizationMembership.Status (per-org — the field VCST-5281 adds: Invited / Approved / Rejected / Deleted) — settable at create (POST /api/customer/organization-memberships), on update (PUT /api/customer/organization-memberships/{id}, full object), AND declarable as a seeded baseline via the optional trailing membership_status column, now present on ALL THREE membership-creating sources (test-data/b2b/organization-memberships.csv — the source for these fixtures — plus test-data/b2b/users.csv and test-data/white-labeling/users.csv, so all 32 seeded memberships can declare one) (legal values Invited | Approved | Rejected | Deleted; blank ⇒ the key is omitted from the create POST and set null on the reconcile PUT, so the effective status inherits the contact's — still the case for all six existing rows MOM-001 to MOM-006). ensureOrgMembership threads status through both create and the reconcile PUT, and npm run td:validate:b2b check [9] hard-fails an illegal status value. Every case here NEVERTHELESS drives the per-org status walk via PUT AS TEST STEPS rather than declaring a seeded baseline: a seeded BLOCKING baseline would make the positive conditions unusable, so the walk belongs in the steps.
  Effective status = ResolveEffectiveStatus(membershipStatus, memberStatus): a non-empty membership status wins, else the contact status, else 'Approved'.
